# CFT pool development comparison

Reuse the 20 OR-Library NRE–NRH matrices already assessed in equal_budget. All 20 are development data. Use seeds 11, 29 and 47, the existing common greedy warm cover and a five-second single-thread process-CPU witness deadline. The primary comparator is the original five-second CFT runner with the same seed and warm start. The candidate calls CFT for a two-second prefix with the same search settings, retaining actual feasible three-phase local incumbents, including solutions outside the globally improving sequence. Recover original column indices through both fixing maps. Select the 12 lowest-cost distinct covers observed by the prefix cutoff, resolving equal costs by first observation. Include the best prefix incumbent, which may be the common warm cover. Restrict a binary HiGHS set-cover model to the union and supply that incumbent. Presolve and branch-and-bound retain default behavior, with one thread, zero MIP relative and absolute gaps and the paired seed.

Three controls reuse the very same prefix output. First return the best prefix incumbent alone. Second replace the other pool columns by a uniform sample of distinct columns outside the best incumbent, preserving pool cardinality. Third release all columns. Both optimization controls use the identical model, seed, warm start and remaining CPU allowance. Shared matrix parsing and the greedy warm start are outside timing. Include the prefix's actual native CPU through return, Python child-launch, output processing, validation, pool construction and model setup in the candidate and control budgets. Reject late witnesses and record solver return times, eligible primal costs, status and whether the restricted optimum was certified by deadline. For the five-second CFT comparator use its established timing convention. Independently verify all native and final witnesses, restrictions, scores and summaries. Report seed-level and instance-median wins, ties and losses with mean paired relative savings against the five-second comparator and each ablation. Treat these results as screening evidence only.
